expectations.text: The position is computed as roughly 27% of expected sales and compared against the one-month checkpoint.
expectations.evidence: "104 / 380 = 27% at one month out."

expectations.text: 40-50% of expected sales at one month out is named as the on-track band.
expectations.evidence: "checkpoint for one month out is 40–50% ... 152–190 tickets"

expectations.text: 27% is placed in the 25-30% band characteristic of a team that skipped or delayed its visibility push - an execution shortfall, not a demand verdict.
expectations.evidence: "lands at 25–30% ... You are inside that band." "points to an execution shortfall"

expectations.text: The response refuses to conclude weak demand from the checkpoint number alone, noting that execution and demand shortfalls have opposite fixes.
expectations.evidence: "The two have opposite fixes"; "Each camp is arguing a conclusion that the single number ... can't support."

expectations.text: It checks whether the 380 figure is net of comps (sponsor, speaker, organizer, volunteer tickets) before trusting the percentage.
expectations.evidence: "If 380 included comps, say 60, then expected sales are 320"; question 1

expectations.text: It checks whether program or speaker announcements ran later than planned.
expectations.evidence: "late program or speaker announcements"

expectations.text: It checks whether the theme is narrow enough to exclude part of the intended audience.
expectations.evidence: "a theme narrow enough to exclude part of your audience"

expectations.text: It checks whether the messaging ever actually said who is welcome, named as a funnel problem rather than a vague promote-more diagnosis.
expectations.evidence: "messaging that never says who is welcome"

expectations.text: Reach signals (registration-page traffic, email opens, partner referrals) are used to discriminate execution shortfall from demand shortfall.
expectations.evidence: Pull page traffic by source, opens/clicks, partner referrals; verdict table by reach

expectations.text: Healthy reach with low conversion is routed to the price or the registration page, not answered with more reach.
expectations.evidence: "Route to event-ticket-pricing or event-landing-page. Don't buy more reach."

expectations.text: Healthy reach and healthy conversion is named as a genuine demand read belonging to the demand-fit diagnosis and the event's own scope-downgrade decision, not to a bigger campaign.
expectations.evidence: "Route to event-market-fit. Right-size the event (Good/Better/Best downgrade)."

expectations.text: The 40% price cut and track cancellation are not endorsed as a first response before the diagnosis.
expectations.evidence: "Do not cancel the track or cut prices this week."

expectations.text: Paid ads are not recommended as a reflex response to the miss.
expectations.evidence: "only after one owned channel shows a tracked signal... A miss alone is not a reason to spend."

expectations.text: The final-two-weeks surge is noted as still ahead and a normal part of the curve.
expectations.evidence: "The final-two-weeks surge is normal, but it can't close this gap"
